signIn.welcome: Welcome. Make the admin account to get started.

tray.title: In the background

subs.checkup: Box Office checks itself for problems you can fix: keys, folders, files, connections, backups and tasks.

getEpisodes.recentOne: The latest aired season, and new ones
getEpisodes.recent_one: The last {{count}} season, and new ones
getEpisodes.recent_other: The last {{count}} seasons, and new ones

log.intro: Box Office keeps its latest log lines, newest first, in memory and in its data folder, so the run before a restart, and how it ended, can be read here too. Download them to attach to a bug report: the download starts with the end of the run before.
log.searchPlaceholder: Search, such as a title, an indexer or an error
log.previousSpan: The run before this one, from {{from}} to {{to}}.
log.crashed: It crashed. This is what Box Office wrote as it did:
log.noCrash: It left no crash behind: it stopped, or something stopped it from outside, such as Kubernetes deleting the pod, running out of memory or a power cut.
log.debugBody: Logs every request, indexer search (with why each release was or wasn't taken), news server connection, download stage and task. Turn it on to find out why something didn't happen, then off again: it's a lot of lines. It stays on across restarts until you turn it off.
log.debugForced: BOXOFFICE_DEBUG is set in the deployment, so it stays on. Remove it and restart Box Office to turn it off.

help.discord1: In Discord, open the channel you want alerts in and click its gear (Edit Channel).
help.discord2: Open Integrations, then Webhooks, and click New Webhook.
help.discord3: Click Copy Webhook URL and paste it here.
help.ntfy1: Pick a long, hard-to-guess topic name, such as boxoffice-7f3k9q2m.
help.ntfy2: Paste https://ntfy.sh/ followed by the topic here (or your own ntfy server instead of ntfy.sh).
help.ntfy3: In the ntfy app on your phone, tap + and subscribe to the same topic.
help.ntfy4: Only if the topic is protected: make an access token in ntfy under Account, and paste it below.
help.ha1: In Home Assistant, open Settings, then Automations & scenes, and click Create automation.
help.ha2: Add a trigger, pick Webhook, and copy the webhook address it shows.
help.ha3: Add the actions you want, such as a notification to your phone, and save.
help.json1: Box Office posts each alert as JSON with its title, message, level, rule, time and server.
help.json2: Paste the address that should receive it, starting with https:// or http://.

alerts.intro: Get an email or a message when something needs you. Alerts go straight from Box Office to your own mail server or webhooks, and nowhere else.
alerts.forwarded: They also show up in Matinee for its admins.
alerts.diskHint: Box Office's data, downloads, backups, or a root folder's disk.
alerts.folder: A root folder can't be read
alerts.folderHint: After 2 minutes, so a network share that drops for a moment doesn't count.
alerts.downloadsHint: Each failed release is blocked and another looked for; this says when that keeps happening.
alerts.restartHint: Says whether it was updated, or stopped without shutting down cleanly.
alerts.backupHint: When a scheduled database backup can't be made.
alerts.problems: The daily look finds problem files
alerts.problemsHint: Only what's new: problems in Settings → Problem files that no earlier look found.
alerts.serverHint: Your email provider's SMTP server, such as smtp.gmail.com or smtp.fastmail.com.
alerts.passwordHint: For Gmail, iCloud and others with two-step sign-in, make an app password in your account's security settings and use that.
alerts.webhooksSub: Post alerts to Discord, ntfy, Home Assistant, or anything else that takes JSON.
alerts.name: Name
alerts.addressKept: The saved address is kept unless you enter a new one.
alerts.token: Access token (only for a protected topic)
alerts.inMatinee: Alerts show up in Matinee. Set up email or a webhook to get them elsewhere too.
alerts.setUp: Set up email or a webhook to get alerts.
alerts.links: Alerts link back to this page once Box Office knows its address, which it learns the next time you open it.
alerts.prometheusSub: For Prometheus, Grafana and other monitoring on your network: the readings on the Server tab, at an address that needs a token.
alerts.k8s: In Kubernetes, Prometheus can reach Box Office at its service address inside the cluster (its service name, namespace and port 7272) instead of the address above.

backups.sub: Everything Box Office knows, in one file: titles, settings, profiles and what came over from other apps. A backup restores into SQLite or PostgreSQL.
backups.remoteError: The second place couldn't be listed: {{error}}
backups.s3: S3-compatible storage (AWS, Backblaze B2, R2, MinIO…)
backups.secretKept: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
backups.pathStyle: Bucket in the path (MinIO usually needs this)
backups.passphraseKept: Backups are encrypted. Leave blank to keep the passphrase.
backups.passphraseHint: Set one to encrypt backups. Keep it somewhere safe: without it a backup cannot be restored.
backups.restoreBody: Everything in Box Office is replaced by the backup's copy. Box Office backs up what's here now first, so this can be undone. Backup settings stay as they are, and everyone signs in again.

music.noneBody: Add an artist and Box Office lists their albums from MusicBrainz. Studio albums are wanted to start with; you can pick EPs, singles and live albums too.
music.placeholder: Artist name, or a MusicBrainz id
music.nobody: MusicBrainz has nobody by that name.
music.noRoot: Add a music root folder under <link>Settings</link> first, so Box Office knows where the music goes.
music.whichHint: You can switch any album on or off later from the artist's page.
music.watch: Watch for new albums of these kinds
music.lookup: Box Office looks the albums up on MusicBrainz, which takes a few seconds for artists with a lot of them.
music.qualityHint: Which copies Box Office looks for. FLAC is lossless and about three times the size of MP3.

qualities.flac-first: FLAC, or MP3 when there's no FLAC

artist.filesAt: Albums go in {{path}}, a folder each. Albums already there are found when you add or refresh the artist, and aren't downloaded again.
artist.watch: Watch for new albums from this artist
artist.kindsHint: Changing these switches every album of that kind on or off below.
artist.noAlbums: MusicBrainz lists no albums for {{name}} yet.

quarantine.title: Quarantine
quarantine.held_one: {{count}} release, {{size}}. Box Office held it because it didn't look safe, and won't open it or move it into the library.
quarantine.held_other: {{count}} releases, {{size}}. Box Office held these because they didn't look safe, and won't open them or move them into the library.
quarantine.stay: They stay until you delete them; you can have them deleted after a number of days in <link>Settings</link>.
quarantine.noReason: Box Office doesn't know why any more: the download it came from was cleared from the history.
quarantine.deleteBody: Their files ({{size}}) are deleted for good. Downloads in the history that they came from stay, and say so.
quarantine.releaseBody: Releasing moves them back into the downloads folder, where they can be downloaded or moved into your library. They may hold a program pretending to be a video; their files can't be run, but only release them if you know what's in them.

files.title: Files
files.locked: {{problem}} Until that's fixed, files can be looked at but not changed.
files.quarantineNote: Downloads that didn't look safe. Box Office won't open, download or move these into the library, and nothing here can run. Delete them, or release one only if you're sure it's fine.
files.inUseHint: {{label}}. You can change this once the download is done.
files.deletesFolder_one: This deletes the folder and everything in it: {{count}} file, {{size}}.
files.deletesFolder_other: This deletes the folder and everything in it: {{count}} files, {{size}}.
files.forGood: It can't be undone. Only the downloads folder is touched; your library isn't.
files.releaseBody: Box Office quarantined this because it didn't look safe: it may hold a program pretending to be a video, or no video at all. Its files can't be run, but releasing it moves it back into the downloads folder, where it can be downloaded or moved into your library.
files.releaseOnly: Only release it if you know what's in it. Moving into the library still only takes video and subtitle files.
files.movesFolder: Box Office moves the main video (and its subtitles) into the title's folder and names it for you, then deletes what's left of the folder. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.moves: Box Office moves the main video (and its subtitles) into the title's folder and names it for you. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.addFromMovies: It has to be in your library first; add it from Movies.
files.addFromShows: It has to be in your library first; add it from Shows.
files.episodeAuto: As its name or tags say
files.episodeNote: Each video goes to the episode its name says, like S01E02. Videos with scrambled names go by the episode summary in their own tags, and any it can't tell stay here for you to choose.
files.movesEbook: Box Office moves the best ebook file (EPUB first) into the author's folder and names it for you. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.movesEbookFolder: Box Office moves the best ebook file (EPUB first) into the author's folder and names it for you, then deletes what's left of the folder. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.movesAudiobook: Box Office moves the audio files, in order, into the book's folder in the author's folder. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.movesAudiobookFolder: Box Office moves the audio files, in order, into the book's folder in the author's folder, then deletes what's left of the folder. A copy already there is set aside, not deleted.
files.addFromBooks: It has to be in your library first; add it from Books, where its author is.
files.addFromAudiobooks: It has to be in your library first; add it from Audiobooks, where its author is.

settings.tmdbIntro: Box Office looks up movies and shows on TMDB. Get a free key at <link>themoviedb.org</link>; the API key and the longer read access token both work.
settings.tmdbBuiltIn: This copy of Box Office comes with the project's own key, so there's nothing to set up. You can still save your own key here to use it instead.
settings.replaceKey: Enter a new key to replace it
settings.moveInSub: Bring everything over from Radarr, Sonarr or NZBGet. The old app is only read from, so it's safe to do again, such as for an app you add later.
settings.matineeSub: In Matinee, go to Settings → Add-ons → Box Office and choose Connect. Matinee looks for Box Office on its own; if it can't find it, enter this address. Then paste the API key. Requests, posters and notifications all go through that one connection.
settings.keyEnv: The key is set on the server (BOXOFFICE_API_KEY), so it's changed there.
settings.moreSub: Turn on the other kinds of media you want Box Office to look after. Each is off until you turn it on, and turning one off later keeps its folders and settings. Box Office never changes files already in these libraries.
settings.pickRoot: Pick a root folder for each one you turned on, below. Adding and searching for these arrives in the next Box Office updates.
settings.noRoots: None yet. Each title gets its own folder inside one of these.

scanFor.movie: Scan looks for movies already in a folder that aren't on the list, so you can add them where they are.
scanFor.series: Scan looks for shows already in a folder that aren't on the list, so you can add them where they are.
scanFor.music: Scan looks for artists already in a folder that aren't on the list, so you can add them where they are.
scanFor.books: Scan looks for authors already in a folder that aren't on the list, so you can add them where they are.
scanFor.game: Check looks through this folder for each system's games, such as roms/mame and roms/snes, and checks them against MAME's and No-Intro's lists. It never changes your files.

settings.newShowsSub: Which episodes Box Office watches for when a show is added, here or by a request from Matinee. A long-running show can have hundreds of old episodes; watching only the last few seasons keeps the library patrol and upgrades on what you're likely to watch. You can still pick something else when adding a show, and switch seasons on or off from the show's page. Shows already on the list keep what they have.
settings.howManyHint: Counts seasons that have started airing; seasons still to come are always watched. A show with this many seasons or fewer gets every season.
settings.recycleSub: When a better copy replaces one, the old copy is set aside in a .recycle folder in its library folder, by the day it was replaced, rather than deleted. To keep one, move it out of there yourself before it's deleted. These copies still take space until they're deleted.
settings.nothingAside: Nothing has been set aside yet.
settings.deleteReplacedHint: Box Office checks every few hours and deletes, for good, copies set aside longer than this.
settings.emptyBody_one: This deletes {{count}} replaced copy ({{size}}) for good, freeing the space. It can't be got back. The copies in your library aren't touched.
settings.emptyBody_other: This deletes {{count}} replaced copies ({{size}}) for good, freeing the space. They can't be got back. The copies in your library aren't touched.
settings.foundOne: Box Office found a folder that looks like your {{name}} library:
settings.foundMany: Box Office found folders that look like your {{name}} library:
settings.lockedProfile: Built in. Box Office never searches for, downloads, upgrades, replaces or deletes the files of titles on it. Put a title on it from its page, or many at once with Select on Movies or Shows.
settings.newHint: At least 8 characters. Every device signs in again.
settings.restartSub: Stops Box Office cleanly and starts it again, for when something seems stuck. Downloads pause where they are and carry on once it's back.

settings.restartDownloads: Downloads running now: {{n}}. They pause where they are and carry on after the restart.
settings.restartingSub: This page reconnects by itself once Box Office is back.
settings.restartSlow: Box Office isn't back yet. If it stays away, look at its logs where it runs, such as the pod's logs in Kubernetes or docker logs.

cap.title: Monthly data cap
cap.sub: If your internet plan has a monthly allowance, Box Office keeps its downloads under it: as the month fills up, upgrades wait first, then automatic searches for missing titles, then downloading itself. Everything carries on when the month starts again.
cap.counts: This counts what Box Office downloads. It can't see the rest of your home's use, so leave room for it.
cap.allowanceHint: 1000 GB is 1 TB. To find yours:
cap.step1: Sign in to your internet provider's website or app.
cap.step2: Open Usage, Data usage or My plan. It shows the monthly allowance (such as 1.2 TB) and the day your month starts.
cap.upgradesAtHint: Better copies of what you have already wait from here.
cap.missingAtHint: From here, Box Office stops searching and grabbing by itself. Downloads you start yourself go on until the cap.
cap.resetDayHint: Your provider's bill or usage page says which day your allowance starts again.

auto.title: Missing titles and upgrades
auto.sub: Box Office finds what's wanted two ways. RSS sync reads each indexer's list of new releases every few minutes, which catches new episodes and movies as they're posted. The library patrol searches every hour for a few monitored titles that have no copy yet (new ones first, then ones missing longer). With Automatic upgrades on, both also look for better copies of files below the quality profile's good-enough quality. A better copy replaces the old one, which is set aside in the library's .recycle folder (see Recycle folders above to free that space).
auto.wantedUpgradesOff: Wanted now: {{missing}}, {{upgrades}} (looked for by themselves only for titles with upgrades turned on).
auto.rssHint: Only while Download releases is on, and for indexers with RSS on. One call to each indexer each time, or up to 5 after a long gap.
auto.everyHint: 15 suits most indexers; 10 is the least.
auto.patrolHint: Only while Download releases is on. Each title waits a day before it's searched again, and longer (up to 30 days) while searches keep finding nothing. A season with 3 or more episodes wanted is searched as one, which can bring a season pack.
auto.upgradesHint: Off by default. When on, RSS sync and the patrol also grab better copies of files below their profile's good-enough quality, for profiles with upgrades on. You can always look for an upgrade yourself from a title's page. Each movie and show can also turn them on or off for itself, from its page.
auto.perMonthHint: 0 means no limit. Counts every upgrade Box Office grabs without you picking it: RSS sync, the patrol, searches when a title is added, and Matinee's search commands. Ones you start from a title's page, or pick with Choose a release, don't count. Starts again on the 1st.
auto.replaceSameHint: On by default. When a copy is reported as broken or in the wrong language, its replacement is the same quality, or the closest one at the same picture size. It's never a bigger picture or a remux, so a 1080p copy doesn't come back as a 2160p remux many times its size. If nothing at that size turns up, a smaller one the quality profile takes will do. Choose a release still lets you pick any.
auto.usedOf: Automatic upgrades this month: {{used}} of {{limit}} used
auto.usedFull: Automatic upgrades this month: all {{limit}} used, so no more until the 1st
auto.usedNoLimit: Automatic upgrades this month: {{count}} (no limit set)
auto.perDayHint: Each search asks every indexer once. The patrol never uses more than half of what an indexer has left for the day, so searches you start yourself always have room. Set your indexer's daily limits under Indexers.

indexers.title: Indexers
indexers.sub: Where Box Office searches for releases.

servers.title: News servers
servers.sub: Your Usenet provider's servers, which downloads come from.

clients.title: Download clients
clients.sub: Other download apps. Box Office downloads Usenet releases itself; these are kept for torrents, which come in a later update.

conn.secretSaved: Saved; type a new one to change it

indexer.addressHint: The indexer's API address. To find it:
indexer.address1: Sign in to the indexer's website.
indexer.address2: Open its API page (often under your profile, or "API" in the menu).
indexer.address3: Copy the API address it gives, like https://api.indexer.example. If it only gives a website, use that.
indexer.addressProwlarr: For an indexer in Prowlarr, use Prowlarr's address for it, like http://prowlarr:9696/1.
indexer.key1: On the indexer's website, open your profile or API page.
indexer.key2: Copy the API key (a long string of letters and numbers) and paste it here.
indexer.keyProwlarr: For an indexer in Prowlarr, it's Prowlarr's own key: Settings, General, API Key.
indexer.answersBoth: It answers, with movie and TV search
indexer.pressTest: Press Test to pick from the indexer's own list. Movies are 2000 and TV is 5000 on nearly every indexer.
indexer.apiPathHint: Nearly always /api, which is used when this is blank. Change it only if the indexer's API page says so.
indexer.priorityHint: 1 to 50. When two indexers have the same release, the lower number wins.
indexer.queriesHint: Your account's daily API limit; 0 if you don't know it.
indexer.grabsHint: Your account's daily NZB download (grab) limit; 0 if you don't know it.
indexer.reported: The indexer reports its own limits ({{searches}} searches, {{grabs}} downloads a day); numbers here take their place.
indexer.findLimits: To find them, open your profile or account page on the indexer's website: it lists the API calls (or API hits) and downloads (or grabs) a day your membership allows. Box Office stays inside them, and fills them in itself for indexers that report them.
indexer.forRssHint: Reads its newest releases every few minutes for anything wanted.

conn.name: Name
conn.nameHint: Leave it blank to name it after its address.

status.errors_one: After {{count}} error in a row, Box Office waits before asking it again, longer each time. Its last answer: {{error}}
status.errors_other: After {{count}} errors in a row, Box Office waits before asking it again, longer each time. Its last answer: {{error}}

server.where: Your Usenet provider's welcome email, or the account page on its website, lists the server address, your username and password, and how many connections your plan allows.
server.hostHint: Like news.newshosting.com. Use the one for your region if your provider lists several.
server.tlsHint: Almost every provider offers it; it stops your internet provider seeing what you download.
server.portHint: 563 for encrypted, 119 for plain, unless your provider says otherwise.
server.passwordHint: Your Usenet account's password, from the provider's welcome email.
server.connectionsHint: Your plan's limit, from your provider's account page. More connections download faster; going over the limit gets connections turned down.
server.useAsHint: A backup server is only asked for articles the main ones don't have, as with a block account.
server.block: It's a block account, or it expires
server.blockHint: A block is an amount of data bought once. Box Office counts what it downloads from it, and stops using it when it runs out or expires.
server.leftHint: In GB, as the provider's account page shows it now. 0 for no limit.
server.expiresHint: The last day it works, from the provider's account page. Blank for never.

client.deluge: Deluge's web interface password: the one you sign in to Deluge's web page with (Preferences, Interface).
client.qbittorrent: qBittorrent's Web UI password (Tools, Options, Web UI).
client.transmission: Transmission's remote access password (Preferences, Remote), if you set one.
client.sabnzbd: In SABnzbd, open Config, General, and copy the API Key.
client.hostHint: The name or IP address of the computer {{app}} runs on, as Box Office reaches it. In Kubernetes, that's usually its service name, like {{service}}.
client.https: Its web address starts with https
client.urlBaseHint: Only if you reach its web page under a path, like /deluge. Usually blank.
client.categoryHint: The label or category Box Office's downloads get in the app, so they're kept apart from others. Several can be given, separated by commas.
client.nameHint: Leave it blank to name it after the app.

blurb.radarr: Movies, their files, quality profiles, indexers, download clients and every other setting.
blurb.sonarr: Shows, seasons, episodes and their files, profiles, indexers, download clients and settings.
blurb.nzbget: News servers with their sign-ins, categories and the rest of its settings.
blurb.lidarr: Artists, their albums and where they are on disk, indexers, download clients and the blocklist.
blurb.readarr: Authors, the books it wants as ebooks or audiobooks and where they are on disk, indexers, download clients and the blocklist.

move.title: Move in
move.sub: Bring everything over from Radarr, Sonarr, Lidarr, Readarr or NZBGet, step by step. The old app is only read from, so nothing in it changes.

look.wait: A large library can take a few minutes. This carries on in the background: you can connect another app or leave this page, and the bell at the top says when it's ready. Nothing changes here or in {{app}} until you confirm on the next step.

connect.notFound: Box Office couldn't find {{app}} by itself. Enter the address you open it at, such as {{example}}. If you open it at an address like https://example.com/{{path}}, keep the /{{path}} at the end. In Kubernetes, use its service name: kubectl get svc -A | grep {{path}} lists it.
connect.nzb1: Open NZBGet and go to Settings, then Security.
connect.nzb2: Copy ControlUsername and ControlPassword here. They're what you sign in to NZBGet with.
connect.key3: Under Security, copy the API Key and paste it above.
connect.onlyReads: This only reads. Nothing changes here or in {{app}} until you confirm on the next step.
connect.lidarrOff: Moving in from Lidarr? Turn on Music under <link>Settings</link> first.
connect.readarrOff: Moving in from Readarr? Turn on Ebooks or Audiobooks under <link>Settings</link> first.

maps.title: Path maps (usually not needed)
maps.hint: Box Office works out where your files are by itself, even if it sees them somewhere else than {{app}} does. Add a map only if the next step says it can't see them: {{app}}'s folder on the left, such as /{{folder}}, and where Box Office sees it on the right, such as /media/{{folder}}.

stat.already: here already, left as they are

review.found: Box Office found where these are by looking for {{app}}'s titles in its own folders. If one is wrong, go back and add a path map.
review.keptHint: Box Office uses indexers, download clients and news servers once its downloader is on. The rest is kept for reference.
review.backupHere: Back up Box Office first, so this can be undone with a restore
review.backupNzb: Save a copy of NZBGet's settings
review.backupApp: Have {{app}} make a backup of itself, and keep it here
review.hidden_one: Needed for the {{count}} password or API key {{app}} hides from other apps.
review.hidden_other: Needed for the {{count}} passwords and API keys {{app}} hides from other apps.
review.nothing: Nothing in {{app}} changes. Files stay where they are.
review.lidarrQuality: Lidarr's quality profiles stay behind: Box Office's music has its own quality setting, under Music.
review.readarrQuality: Readarr's quality profiles stay behind: Box Office picks EPUB for ebooks and M4B for audiobooks first. Each root folder says whether it holds ebooks or audiobooks, worked out from its files.

moving.asItWas: The old app is as it was.
moving.restore: You can restore the backup made first, under Backups.

matinee.title: Point Matinee at Box Office <muted>(optional)</muted>
matinee.only: Only if you watch with Matinee. If you use Plex, Jellyfin, Emby or another player, skip this: the move-in is already done, and nothing else depends on it. You can also do it later.
matinee.how: Matinee's {{app}} connection moves to Box Office, keeping its quality profile and root folder. Matinee checks the new connection before saving it, so a wrong address changes nothing. Your Matinee sign-in is used once and not kept.
matinee.ours: Box Office's address, as Matinee reaches it
matinee.oursHint: Inside Kubernetes this is usually the service, such as http://boxoffice:7272.
matinee.later: Skip, I'll do it later or I don't use Matinee

done.title: Moved in from {{app}}
done.switched: Matinee's {{app}} connection now goes to {{after}} (it was {{before}}).
done.stillUses: If you watch with Matinee, it still uses {{app}}. When you're ready, point it at Box Office from here or in Matinee's admin settings, using the address and API key under <link>Settings</link>.
done.shutDown: You can shut down {{app}} now. Box Office keeps its backup under <link>Backups</link> in case you need anything from it.
done.backsUp: From here on, Box Office backs itself up. Send backups to another folder or cloud storage under Backups.

overview.fresh: Starting fresh, with nothing to move in from? <button>Skip moving in</button> and Move in leaves the menu. It stays under Settings if you need it later.
overview.notMoved: Not moved in. Skip it if you never used it.
overview.notSwitched: Not switched over. Only needed if you watch with Matinee.
overview.lives: Move in now lives under Settings. You can still move in from an app you add later.
overview.showAgain: Show Move in in the menu again
overview.finishHint: Once everything you use has come over. Move in then leaves the menu, and stays under Settings.

skip.skipped: Skipped. Nothing comes over from it, and it's not asked for again.
skip.offer: Don't use {{app}}? <button>Skip it</button>, and Move in stops asking for it. You can undo that.
skip.isSkipped: You skipped {{app}}. You can still move in from it, or <button>undo the skip</button>.

dl.title: Downloads
dl.nothingHint: Releases Box Office grabs show up here. You can also add an NZB file yourself.
dl.missingHint: Releases that can't be used: too incomplete on the news servers to repair, or locked with a password the release didn't give. Box Office blocked each one and looked for another, so there's nothing to do.

turnOn.title: Downloading is off
turnOn.sub: Box Office downloads from Usenet itself, in place of NZBGet. It's off until you turn it on, so it never competes with the apps you're moving from. Searches still run, and Activity says what they found.
turnOn.step1: Add your Usenet provider under News servers in Settings.
turnOn.step2: Check your indexers in Settings; each needs its API key.
turnOn.step3: Turn on downloading in Settings, under Downloads.

dl.waitingLibrary: Waiting to go into the library
dl.staysQuarantined: Its files stay in quarantine at {{path}}; delete or release them under Quarantine below. Don't open them.
dl.alsoDelete: Also delete its files in the downloads folder
dl.neverTouched: Files already moved into your library are never touched.

req.title: Requests
req.sub: What people asked for on the request site, and the problems they found.
req.off: The request site is turned off. Turn it on under <link>Request site</link>.

list.newShowHere: New requests from the request site show up here.
list.onceAsked: Once people ask for titles on the request site, they show up here.

approve.title: Approve {{title}}
approve.noMovieRoot: Add a root folder for movies under Settings first.
approve.noShowRoot: Add a root folder for shows under Settings first.

decline.title: Decline {{title}}
decline.whyHint: Optional. {{member}} sees it under My requests.

problems.empty: When someone reports a problem with a title on the request site, it shows up here.

fix.title: Fixed: {{title}}
fix.how: To swap a bad file, open the title and use Choose a release or Search; then mark the problem fixed here.

people.sub: People who can sign in to the request site. They can't open this admin UI.
people.empty: Add people here, let them make their own accounts, or let them sign in with Matinee, under Request site.
people.name: Name

person.usernameHint: What they sign in with. No spaces.
person.nameHint: Optional. What the request site calls them.
person.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Pass it on to them; they can change it on the request site.
person.moviesWeekHint: Empty follows the site; 0 is no limit.
person.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep theirs. Setting one signs them out.
person.matinee: They sign in with their Matinee account, so their password is set in Matinee.

site.title: The request site
site.sub: A site of its own for the people who watch: they find movies and shows, ask for them, follow how it's going, and report problems.
site.addressHint: Share this with the people who use it.
site.hostHint: Optional, such as requests.example.com. Point that name at Box Office (in DNS and your ingress or reverse proxy), and there the request site is the whole site. This admin UI stays at its usual address.
site.welcomeHint: Shown on the sign-in page and at the top of Discover.
site.colourHint: Buttons, links and highlights. Empty uses Box Office's red.
site.logoHint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 512 KB. Shown in place of the ticket.
site.matineeHint: To let people sign in with their Matinee account: the address you open Matinee at, such as http://matinee.local:7171. Box Office checks their password with Matinee. Leave it empty to turn this off.
site.signUp: Let people make their own account
site.approvalHint: Each person can have their own setting, under People.
site.seasons: Approved shows watch the seasons set under Settings → New shows.

problems.title: Problem files
problems.sub: Files in the movie and TV library folders that need a hand. Nothing changes until you press a fix, and the originals wait in the library's .recycle/problem-files folder until you delete them or put them back.
problems.cardSub: Find what's out of place in the movie and TV library folders: files that aren't on the list, extra copies, disc images, movies in parts and untidy names, and fix them once you've checked what each fix does.
problems.next: Looks again by itself every day, next {{when}}.
problems.none: Nothing needs a hand: everything is where it should be.
problems.unreadable: Box Office can't read {{path}}, or it's empty (a share that isn't mounted?), so it was left out.
problems.readOnly: {{path}} is read-only for Box Office, so what's in it is listed but can't be fixed.
problems.noFFmpeg: FFmpeg isn't installed where Box Office runs, so disc images can't be remuxed and parts can't be joined.
problems.remuxNote: (a copy of the streams, nothing re-encoded)
problems.copiesNote: Each of these runs as long as a whole movie, so they look like copies (another cut or quality), not parts. Pick the one to keep, or join them if they really are parts.

blocked.readOnly: The library folder is read-only for Box Office.
blocked.outputExists: There's a file where the fixed one would go already.

detail.foundFolder: its folder, named differently on disk

duplicate.title: More than one copy
duplicate.hint: Pick the copy to keep. The others are set aside, and the one kept is recorded as the title's copy.

parts.title: Movies in parts
parts.hint: Parts named CD1, CD2, Part 1… are joined into one MKV without re-encoding. The parts are set aside once the new file is checked.

discImage.title: Disc images
discImage.hint: The movie on a DVD or Blu-ray image (its longest title) is copied into an MKV without re-encoding, and the image is set aside once the new file is checked. A show's disc or an image that isn't any title's can only be set aside.

untracked.title: Copies Box Office doesn't know
untracked.hint: Videos in a title's folder, or loose and named for a title, that Box Office hasn't recorded. Fixing records each as the title's copy, renamed the way Box Office names things.

missing.title: Missing files
missing.hint: Box Office has these as titles' copies, but they're gone from disk. Forgetting them lets Box Office look for the titles again.

naming.title: Names and folders
naming.hint: Renamed to Title (Year), with episodes in Season folders as Title (Year) - S01E02 - Episode. Subtitles go along. Names that start like that and add tags such as the quality are left as they are.

unknown.title: Videos that aren't an episode
unknown.hint: Videos in a show's folder that aren't named for one of its episodes.

notListed.title: Not on the list
notListed.hint: Folders and videos that aren't any title on the list. They're often movies or shows Box Office doesn't know yet: add them with Scan. Set one aside only when you're sure you don't want it.

leftover.title: Leftovers
leftover.hint: Samples, programs, shortcuts, and what's left of downloads and archives.

editions.title: Different cuts of a movie
editions.hint: These copies run for very different lengths or are named for different cuts, so they aren't duplicates. Keeping them all records each other cut as an edition, named with an {edition-…} tag that Matinee, Plex and Jellyfin read. Nothing is set aside.

waiting.title: Set aside, waiting for your OK
waiting.sub: Set aside means moved out of the library into its .recycle/problem-files folder. Nothing has been deleted, but until you put them back, Plex, Matinee and Box Office don't see them. Put back returns each to where it was; Delete for good frees the space. Emptying the recycle folders leaves them alone.
waiting.confirmBody: This deletes {{count}} set aside ({{size}}) from the recycle folder. It can't be undone.

notListed.title: No title on the list matched them
notListed.hint: Often movies or shows Box Office doesn't know yet, or knows by a garbled name. Put them back, then add them with Scan. Delete only what you're sure you don't want.

secondFolder.title: A second folder for a title
secondFolder.hint: The title's own folder is still in the library. Check this one holds nothing it lacks before deleting.

unknown.title: Videos in a show's folder that weren't an episode
unknown.hint: Look before deleting: one may be a special or an episode with an odd name.

duplicate.title: Extra copies
duplicate.hint: The copy you kept is still in the library and recorded. These are the others.

parts.title: Parts of joined movies
parts.hint: The joined MKV is in the library and was checked. These are the parts it was made from.

discImage.title: Disc images
discImage.hint: Where an image was remuxed, the new MKV is in the library. A show's disc or an image that wasn't any title's was only set aside.

leftover.title: Leftovers
leftover.hint: Samples, shortcuts, programs, and what's left of downloads (.nzb, .par2, archives). Safe to delete.

other.title: Renamed and recorded
other.hint: Nothing was set aside. These only wait for you to say they look right.

problems.garbledName: The name on disk is garbled; it's meant to be “{{name}}”.

ereaders.title: Send to e-readers
ereaders.intro: Box Office can email ebooks to your Kindle, your PocketBook, or any reader with its own email address: by itself as each one downloads, or from a book's page.
ereaders.name: Name
ereaders.addressHint: Its Send to Kindle or Send-to-PocketBook address. Below says where to find it.
ereaders.autoHint: Each ebook Box Office downloads goes to this reader once it's in the library. Books already on disk aren't sent.
ereaders.where: Where do I find a {{kind}}'s address?
ereaders.kindleFormats: Kindles take EPUB and PDF by email, but not AZW3 or MOBI. To have those turned into EPUB before they're sent, add Calibre's ebook-convert to Box Office (see the guide).
ereaders.kobo: Kobo, Tolino and Boox readers can't receive books by email, so Box Office can't send to them.
ereaders.sameAsAlerts: Use the mail server from Health → Alerts
ereaders.sameAsAlertsHint: Books go out through {{host}}, like alerts do.
ereaders.noAlertMail: There's no mail server under Health → Alerts yet. Set one up there, or enter one below.
ereaders.setUpAlerts: Set up email in Health → Alerts
ereaders.fromSameHint: Leave it empty to use the address alerts come from. It must be one your mail server lets you send as.
ereaders.fromHint: Usually the same as the username. It must be one your mail server lets you send as.
ereaders.usernameHint: Your email address, for most providers. Gmail and iCloud fill in the server for you.
ereaders.passwordHint: For Gmail and iCloud, an app password, not your usual one. See the steps below.
ereaders.filledIn: Filled in for your email provider.
ereaders.approve: Add this address to your reader's approved senders, or it won't take the books:
ereaders.sentAuto: {{title}} to {{reader}}, by itself after it downloaded
ereaders.sent: Sent to {{reader}}. It can take a few minutes to show up.
ereaders.setUp: Set up sending ebooks to your e-reader

help.kindle1: On a computer, go to Amazon's Manage Your Content and Devices page (amazon.com/myk, or your country's Amazon site) and sign in.
help.kindle2: Open Preferences, then Personal Document Settings.
help.kindle3: Under Send-to-Kindle E-Mail Settings, copy your Kindle's address (it ends in @kindle.com) and paste it here.
help.kindle4: Under Approved Personal Document E-mail List, choose Add a new approved e-mail address and add {{from}}.
help.kindle5: Send a test book. If Amazon emails {{from}} asking you to verify it, open that email and choose Verify Request.
help.pocketbook1: On your PocketBook, open Settings, then Accounts and Synchronization, then Send-to-PocketBook.
help.pocketbook2: Sign in or make an account. Your reader's address ends in @pbsync.com: paste it here.
help.pocketbook3: Add {{from}} to the approved senders there, or approve it from the email PocketBook sends the first time a book arrives.
help.other1: Find the email address your reader or reading app takes books at, in its settings or help pages.
help.other2: Paste it here, and allow {{from}} to send to it if the reader asks you to.
help.mail1: Gmail: type your Gmail address as the username and the server fills itself in. Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account, then make an app password at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords and paste it as the password.
help.mail2: iCloud Mail: type your iCloud address as the username. Make an app-specific password at account.apple.com, under Sign-In and Security, and paste it as the password.
help.mail3: Another provider: its help pages list its outgoing (SMTP) server and port. Usually 587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with TLS.
help.mail4: Books come from the address you send as, so that's the one to approve on your reader.

qualityCheck.title: Quality check
qualityCheck.sub: Box Office looks inside each movie and episode file to see how big its picture really is, and corrects qualities that were guessed wrong from a name. Files with no quality get the closest one their profile takes. Files are only read, never changed. Where a copy came from can't be seen inside a file, so a guess never sets off an upgrade: only a picture that's really smaller makes a copy rank lower.
qualityCheck.noFFprobe: ffprobe isn't installed where Box Office runs, so files can't be looked inside.
qualityCheck.correctedFrom: Corrected from {{was}} after looking inside the file

reported.title: Reported in Matinee: {{what}}.
reported.audio: the sound is broken or out of sync
reported.fixing: Box Office blocked that copy's release and is getting another.

editions.title: Editions of {{title}}
editions.sub: Editions the indexers have, named in their releases. Get one to keep next to the copy you have, or in its place. Box Office never looks for editions by itself.
editions.none: The indexers have no release of it named for an edition, like Extended or Director's Cut.
editions.asked: Looking for the {{edition}} now; see Activity.
editions.otherHint: Not listed? Pick one and Box Office looks for it now, the same way.

games.noneBody: Box Office shows the games you have, arcade sets for MAME and console games such as Super Nintendo and Game Boy, and checks each one without changing it. It can also find games you want and download them.
games.addRoot: Add the folder your games are in under <link>Settings → Games root folders</link>.
games.noSystemsBody: Box Office didn't find any game systems in your games root folders. Put each system's games in a folder named for it, such as mame or snes, then Check again.
games.unsure_one: Box Office couldn't tell which system this folder is for
games.unsure_other: Box Office couldn't tell which system these folders are for
games.unsureHint: Rename each one to the system's name, such as mame, snes, n64 or gba, then Check again.
games.lockedHint: Box Office won't look at {{name}}'s games again until you turn this off, and keeps what it found last time. Use it while you're reorganizing the folder.
games.mameVersionSub: MAME's sets change with each version, so a set that works in one may not in another.
games.mameVersionHint: Pick the MAME version you play with. Box Office downloads that version's list from MAME's releases on GitHub and checks every set again.
games.noGamesBody: Box Office didn't find any games in {{path}}.

explain.missingArcade: Some files this set needs aren't there, so MAME may not start it.
explain.wrongArcade: Some files are from another version of MAME than {{list}}. Pick the version you play with under MAME version, or update the set.
explain.biosArcade: The set itself is complete, but it needs a BIOS or device set that isn't in the folder.
explain.unknownArcade: {{list}} has no set called {{name}}. It may have been renamed since, or be for another emulator.
explain.unreadableArcade: The file can't be opened. It may be damaged, or still being copied.
explain.missing: Some files this game needs aren't there.
explain.wrong: The file is named like a game on No-Intro's list, but isn't the same: a bad copy, or one changed since.
explain.bios: The game needs a BIOS that isn't there.
explain.unknown: No-Intro's list has no copy like this one. It may be a hack, a translation or a homemade game, which is fine.
explain.unreadable: The file can't be opened. It may be damaged, or still being copied.

problem.diskWrong: The {{name}} CHD is from another version

games.noFiles: Its files aren't there any more. Check again to update the list.
games.readOnly: Box Office only reads these files. It never moves, renames or deletes them.

add.title: Add a game
add.sub: Find a game on its system's list. Box Office looks for it on your indexers, downloads it, checks it's the right game and puts it in your games folder.
add.placeholder: Search for a game, such as Super Metroid
add.looking: Looking through the lists… The first search on a system downloads its list, which can take a minute.
add.hint: Search by title. Box Office looks through No-Intro's list of console games and MAME's list of arcade games, for the systems you have folders for. Pick a system to look at another.
add.nothing: No games on the list match.
add.more: Showing the first 60. Add a word to narrow it down.
add.cardSub: Search the list of every game for a system, and Box Office downloads the ones you want.

wanted.title: Wanted
wanted.sub: Box Office looks for these on your indexers every hour, and checks each download against the system's list before it goes in your games folder.
wanted.movedIn: Moved in. Checking the system's folder…
wanted.waiting: Downloaded, and waiting to go in your games folder; see Downloads.
wanted.nothing: Looked {{when}} and found nothing yet. Box Office keeps looking.
wanted.lookingNow: Looking for it now; see Activity.

importFiles.title: Import files
importFiles.sub: Add movies, episodes, music, books or games you already have. Box Office works out what each one is and files it in your library.
importFiles.emptyBody: Upload files or a whole folder from this device, or pick them from a folder on the server. You can also drop files on this page.
importFiles.emptyHint: Name things the usual way, such as “The Matrix (1999).mkv”, “Show S01E02.mkv”, “Artist - Album” or “Author - Title.epub”, and Box Office gets most of them right on its own.
importFiles.waitingHint: Check what Box Office thinks each one is, then import them. Change anything it got wrong.
importFiles.where: Files wait in {{folder}} until they're imported.
importFiles.removeAsk: Remove {{name}} from the imports folder? Box Office deletes its copy. Anything you picked from the server stays where it was.
importFiles.serverHint: Tick the files and folders to import. Box Office copies them, so the originals stay where they are.
importFiles.copyNote: Big folders take a while to copy; you can leave this page meanwhile.
importFiles.lookAgain: Have Box Office look at it again as this kind, or find it below.
importFiles.systemHint: The machine the game is for. In a folder, files that say their system themselves, such as .sfc or .gba, still go to their own system.
importFiles.albumHint: The album's title as MusicBrainz has it, such as “Abbey Road”. Then find the artist below.
importFiles.bookHint: The book's title as Open Library has it, such as “Pride and Prejudice”. Then find the author below.
importFiles.partFirst: Fill in the title above first.
